title: Polyglot client contracts for incremental tool invocations and structured outputs
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Motivation: provide a single, small compatibility layer and canonical interfaces across TypeScript, Python, and Go SDKs to support: 1) incremental (streamed) model outputs with interleaved tool/function call events, 2) typed/structured output envelopes (JSON-schema validated), and 3) graceful migration for legacy clients that expect a non-streamed single JSON response.

Scope: design and ship the SDK surface and example snippets for: InvocableTool contract, FramedEnvelope protocol (type tag + seq + payload), StructuredOutput type helpers (json-schema validation + typed parsing), and a backward-compatibility polyfill that rehydrates streamed envelopes into a single final payload.

Out-of-scope: language-specific full SDK packaging, telemetry schema changes, and console UI work (separate follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: TS/Py/Go SDKs expose a stable InvocableTool interface with examples that compile/run in CI
Streaming response examples demonstrate interleaved tool invocation events and final structured payload for all three languages
Compatibility polyfill helper available that converts a framed stream to a final JSON object for legacy clients
Schema validation helper that can be wired into runtime to validate final structured outputs and surface clear validation errors
Security review completed and no P0 issues outstanding (KMS/hash integrity checks for envelopes documented)
decisions: Use a minimal FramedEnvelope protocol: {type: string, seq: int, payload: <opaque>} for all streamed messages to keep parsers deterministic and enable resumability.
Define InvocableTool interface with 3 core hooks: prepare(context), invoke(payload) -> stream-of-envelopes, finalize(status). This maps naturally to async iterators in TS/Py and channels in Go.
Adopt JSON Schema (draft-07) for structured output contracts. SDKs will include lightweight validators; heavier validation can be opt-in.
Provide a forward-compatible polyfill: stream->reduce that emits identical final object shape for non-streaming clients and exposes partials via callback for progressive apps.
Keep wire protocol text-based (newline-delimited JSON envelopes) to maximize compatibility with proxies and existing infra. Binary framing deferred to future iteration.
Do not change server-side route semantics; server will continue to set Content-Type and a header X-RW-Stream=framed to opt clients into framed mode.
tasks: Spike: implement prototype TS/Py/Go toy servers and clients (done)
Design: finalize envelope shape & error model (done)
Implement: add InvocableTool interfaces and helper adapters in TypeScript SDK
Implement: add matching interfaces and examples in Python SDK
Implement: Go SDK idiomatic bindings (channels + context) and examples
Doc: write migration guide and code snippets for library consumers
Tests: add interop tests that run server in docker and exercise all language clients
Security: complete KMS signing/verification doc and threat model writeup
comments: 2026-02-26 - Aisha Kumar: Spike complete. Implemented toy runtime that emits three envelope types: 'token', 'tool_call', 'final'. Observed stable parsing across node and python streaming parsers.
2026-03-01 - Liam O'Connor: Draft TS interfaces pushed to PR #1428. Please review naming on 'InvocableTool.prepare' vs 'setup' — leaning to 'prepare' for parity with other runtimes.
2026-03-02 - Design (Maya Chen): Feedback: require explicit schema_version field in final payload envelopes to support future schema migration; added to spec.
2026-03-03 - Security (Ravi Patel): Reviewed header model. Request: include HMAC of envelope sequence for tamper detection when using public proxies. Added to security task list.

2026-03-04 - QA (Sofia Nguyen): Interop tests failing intermittently for large loads (sequence reordering seen under concurrency). Root cause: our toy server used non-atomic buffered writes; fixed in prototype and re-running benchmarks.
2026-03-05 - Liam O'Connor: Opened cross-language interop CI job. Included simple 'rehydrate' polyfill test that asserts parity between non-streamed vs rehydrated streamed outputs.
2026-03-06 - Aisha Kumar: Preparing for review. Noted trade-off: newline-delimited JSON loses binary efficiency but is operationally simpler; will revisit after adoption.
2026-03-06 - Product (Carlos Rivera): Approved rollout plan for beta SDKs to internal customers (Platform team) before public release.
release_notes: Introduces experimental framed streaming protocol for tool invocations and structured outputs across TS/Py/Go SDKs.
Includes a compatibility polyfill to convert streams into final JSON objects for legacy clients.
Beta: enabled via X-RW-Stream header; opt-in for now.
